energy_oil.rationale: Facts: OPEC+ (seven countries) held December targets at September levels (~31.01 mb/d) for a third straight month; Brent fell 8.7% to $94.62 on Nov 4 after Democrats won both chambers in the US midterms and the White House tied the losses to the Iran war; Gulf crude flows are recovering toward pre-war levels and JP Morgan flags a possible 1.1 mb/d surplus. Offsets: US commercial crude stocks fell a fifth straight week, distillates are 13% below the 5-year average (below 100m bbl for the first time since 2003), the SPR is at its lowest since 1982 and Asian reserve refills may put a floor under prices. Interpretation: the war risk premium is eroding and political pressure favours de-escalation, a mild headwind for crude and energy equities over 1-3 months, but escalation risk (Eurasia Group 60% odds of renewed US strikes, ongoing Gulf ship incidents) keeps this from -2.

materials_mining_metals.rationale: Facts: LME copper was on course for its worst week since March (-3.4%, ~$13,663/t on Nov 6), with CRU linking the drop to post-midterm AI/data-centre sentiment; at the same time SHFE copper stocks fell 24% in a week to a near three-year low and Shanghai spot premiums hit a record RMB 2,615/t as smelter output fell and metal moved to the US ahead of possible refined-copper tariffs. Lithium carbonate spot hit new lows (Mysteel, Nov 2) amid supply additions and soft demand. Interpretation: weaker demand sentiment (AI capex, lithium) is balanced by very tight physical copper supply, so the net 1-3 month signal for miners is neutral.

gold_precious.rationale: Facts: spot gold rebounded from a one-year low of $3,869.85 (Oct 30) to ~$4,100 on Nov 5 (+3.4% on Nov 4) as the dollar and 10-year yield fell after the midterms and lower oil eased inflation fears; Poland's central bank reached its 700t reserve target and left the door open to more buying. Against that, October payrolls rose 165k vs ~59-65k expected and unemployment fell to 4.1%, and CME FedWatch priced ~66% odds of a December Fed hike (Fed at 3.75-4.00% after a 10-2 hold on Oct 28); gold slipped back to ~$4,070 on Nov 6 while silver held ~$52. Interpretation: a hiking Fed and gold being one of 2026's weakest assets offset the softer dollar and steady official demand; neutral.

commodities_broad.rationale: Facts: energy, the largest weight in broad indices, lost its war premium this week (WTI December -$13, Brent down almost $15 week on week); the Bloomberg Commodity Spot Index fell 2.04% on Nov 4. Grains are soft on supply: CBOT soybeans hit an 11-week low as Chinese buying slowed against a record US crop and fast Brazilian planting, and wheat fell to a six-month low (WEAT). Copper had its worst week since March. Interpretation: falling energy premium plus ample grain supply and a likely December Fed hike are a mild headwind for broad commodity baskets; tight oil products, tight physical copper and Middle East escalation risk limit the downside.

regime_notes: The dominant driver this week was the US midterm result: Democrats took both chambers, the White House blamed the Iran war and gasoline prices, and markets priced faster de-escalation, knocking Brent from ~$106 on Monday to ~$93-95 midweek before a partial rebound to ~$98. Geopolitical risk is not resolved (Gulf ship incidents continue, Eurasia Group sees 60% odds of renewed US strikes), and physical product markets remain very tight, so oil is volatile around a shrinking risk premium. The Fed is in a hiking cycle (3.75-4.00%, ~66% odds of a December hike), and Friday's strong payrolls reinforced that, a headwind for gold and for non-yielding commodities broadly, partly offset by a softer dollar earlier in the week. Copper shows a split between weaker AI/data-centre demand sentiment and record-tight Chinese physical supply, with tariff-driven flows into the US distorting regional stocks. Grains are heavy on record US soybean supply and slower Chinese buying; lithium remains in a supply-driven slump.

red_flags.issue: Possible US tariff on refined copper imports is pulling metal into the US and draining stocks elsewhere; COMEX vs LME/SHFE basis and roll yield may diverge sharply from global copper fundamentals. Not a fund-specific event; monitor tracking.
